scope: One original native s1_module seed17 synthetic fixture; operator forward plus complete VJP. Not a training-quality or global-release gate.
fixture: benchmark_native_deconv.cpu_data(CASES['s1_module'], seed=17), verified against immutable native_baseline.json config and tensor hashes
oracle: Independent original full-FFT converse2d_reference evaluated in FP64 on the same FP32-rounded input, weight, bias and upstream, with native circular pad2/slice crop2
baseline: Original full-FFT converse2d_reference evaluated in FP32 on that same fixture
acceptance: For every tensor, candidate max_abs <= baseline max_abs AND candidate relative_l2 <= baseline relative_l2 against the same FP64 oracle. All values must be finite. No tolerance, percentage, margin or rounding-floor credit is added.
pointwise: Original output 3e-5/3e-5 and VJP 5e-5/5e-5 comparisons against FP64 and Python FP32 are diagnostics only, not acceptance gates
representation_floor: FP64 oracle rounded to FP32, then compared with the FP64 oracle; diagnostic only and never added to the gate
selection: Exclude each failing production/candidate route from timing independently. A failing production control does not block passing candidates. Always retain failed metrics. Python FP32 and native_dense are timed as local baselines after finite/shape checks.
native: Native dense ConvTranspose2d has different mathematics, boundary conditions, bias semantics and parameter count; it is a timing target, not a quality-equivalent solver
release: Local numerical noninferiority alone does not establish model accuracy, training quality, convergence, broader-shape coverage or production eligibility
